analysis.title: Democratic sweep and Riksbank decision (Nordic Alert)
key_insights: Democrats won both the US House and Senate. SEB expects fiscal policy to end in stalemate because Trump, who has announced he intends to be 'Mr. Veto', must sign any Democratic economic reforms.

Trump keeps substantial influence over foreign and trade policy. Middle East developments remain a key factor for the world economy and markets. The White House has pushed for both escalation and renewed negotiations.

Initial market reaction to the Democratic sweep was small: lower US yields, a weaker dollar and lower stock futures. Futures point to a negative open in Europe and the US, and Japan saw larger declines in Asia.

Democratic gains are expected to bring more scrutiny and regulation of the AI sector. Data centre buildout was a prominent campaign issue in Georgia and Texas, and Democrats were declared winners in both states.

Yesterday, US-Iran headlines made oil and gas prices fall quickly, then bounce back after conflicting reports from Iranian sources. A strong JOLTS release lifted government bond yields modestly. The Nasdaq closed up 0.8% and European equities closed slightly lower.
Today's calendar: Riksbank rate decision, European inflation, Norwegian home prices, US services ISM, and the US Treasury quarterly borrowing report in the afternoon.

Most respondents in SEB's investor and trading room surveys expect the Riksbank to raise the policy rate today. The open question is whether the Executive Board is unanimous. Göran Hjelm, and possibly Aino Bunge, may enter reservations. Any dissents will be announced today, and the minutes are published next week.

Swedish household vulnerability argues for caution. About 80% of households have floating-rate mortgages, against roughly 50% in 2022. Energy prices are surging this winter while underlying inflation is subdued and the labour market is cool.
SEB's trading room survey points to limited market reaction if the Riksbank hikes and signals risks to the rate path broadly unchanged from September, which is SEB's main scenario.

If the Riksbank signals greater upside or downside risks, traders expect market rates to move 3-6 basis points and the krona about four figs. Markets price over 90% odds of a hike today and almost 90 basis points of further hikes over the coming year.

Nordic Outlook updates: Danish growth accelerates on very high export growth, and DKK strength lowers the probability of rate hikes. Norway's mainland activity is expected to stabilise in 2027-2028 after a weak first half, and Norges Bank is expected to keep rates elevated until the end of next year.

tension_points.bull_case: A hike today is near certain, and SEB's main scenario is a signal of broadly unchanged risks to the rate path from September, which would bring a limited market reaction.
tension_points.bear_case: Hjelm, and possibly Bunge, may dissent or reserve against the degree of tightening. Households carry high floating-rate mortgage debt, energy prices are surging, underlying inflation is subdued and the labour market is cool.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Riksbank signal of greater upside or downside risks to the policy rate path versus September, or announced dissents, would move market rates 3-6 basis points and the krona about four figs.
